newsitem.title: TURKEY: Tofas to halt production two weeks.
newsitem.headline: Tofas to halt production two weeks.

text.p: Turkey's leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi, equally owned by Italy's Fiat Auto and Koc Holding said it would halt production for two weeks from Tuesday due to demand which narrowed sharply amid expectations of cheaper car imports.

"A decision has been made to halt production for two weeks starting from September 24 in our Bursa plant where 4,800 people are employed," the joint statement by general managers of Tofas and its distributing arm Tofas Oto Ticaret said.

"Rumours and expectations of tax-free imports and have caused the domestic market (sales) to narrow by 30-40 percent when compared to the previous years. We aim to get over this storm by temporarily halting production," it added.
Car and parts producers as well as labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector have recently been angered by government plans to ease car imports.

The government is working on a decree to allow Turkish workers abroad who open a minimum 50,000 mark, one-year savings account in Turkey to bring in cars with a maximum age of four years without paying customs duties. The workers who open such accounts will also benefit from a 20 percent reduction in taxes when buying locally made cars.
The move is part of the government's two disclosed resource packages aiming to raise $10 billion each to fight deficits.
Turkish car producers have not worked at full capacity due to slack domestic demand which barely enlivened since Turkey's 1994 economic crisis.
The automotive sector was the worst hit by the crisis in 1994 when total motor vehicle production slumped by 41 percent.
Car output which rose by only 10 percent to 233,414 last year, stood at 137,074 in the first eight months of 1996, versus 135,905 in the same 1995 period.
Tofas had recently said its export orders fell sharply in September in comparison to previous months, mainly due to competition from Fiat's new model Marea.
Tofas, the sole producer of Fiat's Tempra model since March 1995, has been exporting them for Fiat, but the export agreement will end on December 31.
Tofas made 71,393 cars in January-August, compared to 70,564 in the same 1995 period. Its exports were 27,437 units and domestic sales were 15,446 in the first eight months.
Tofas said it would put all its workers through a technical training programme during the two-week stoppage. -- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
